headline: The container image picks up an OpenSSL denial-of-service fix
summary: A high-severity OpenSSL flaw was disclosed after the previous release shipped, so the image that release was built on carries it. The pinned base now names a rebuild with the patched packages. The vendored framework moves forward eleven releases alongside it, and the pins on every action the release workflows call are brought current.

items.title: Rebuild on a base image with the patched OpenSSL
items.body: CVE-2026-14456 is a denial of service through unbounded memory in OpenSSL, affecting the libcrypto3 and libssl3 packages at 3.6.3-r4 and fixed upstream in 3.6.3-r5. It was disclosed after v1.0.14 was built, so that image scanned clean when it shipped and does not now. The pinned digest now names the Chainguard rebuild carrying the patch.

items.title: What the base pin does and does not reach
items.body: The pin governs the container image. The signed platform binaries are built from the Node runtime they embed rather than from this image, so the change does not alter them.

items.title: Vendored framework moves to blamejs 0.18.50
items.body: Eleven releases forward from 0.18.39. Nothing in that range changes what this client does. The fixes land on session cookie writing, request filtering, mail authentication and filtering, hostname canonicalization, a durable queue, a Markdown renderer, and pattern matching in JSON Schema and JSONPath, and this client calls none of them. The bump keeps it on the same framework version as the server, which the two share for anything crossing the wire.

items.title: Action pins brought current
items.body: Every action the release and container workflows call is pinned to the commit of its latest release; several had fallen behind, among them the code-scanning action. Those workflows produce the binaries the updater fetches and the image operators pull, which is the one place a republished tag would reach a user.
